decision.next_allowed_work: Only consider a new DS4 up/gate source edit if it reuses the accepted one-stream gate cache or avoids duplicating gate storage, provides a DS4-specific parallel/fused compute microbench, and has a hard bound showing simultaneous gate/updown reduction near the ~90% threshold. Plain GGML_MOE_STREAM_FUSED_UP_GATE or one-stream gate+up sharing remains rejected.
decision.reason: Existing DeepSeek4 fused up/gate path already proved CUDA acceptance but was far slower (0.5-0.8 tok/s) and had TTFT regressions. The failure was structural: it either used a tiny zero-hit batch cache or consumed the large gate-cache budget and still ran serial up then gate compute. Re-running a short probe would not add new evidence.

source_notes.cuda_batch_guard: ggml_cuda_moe_stream_up_gate_batch accepts DS4 type only through generic moe_stream_type_supported; current fast parallel branch is restricted to same-type IQ2_S, so DS4 MXFP4/F8 does not get the Kimi parallel fast path.
source_notes.graph_builder: src/llama-graph.cpp constructs ggml_moe_up_gate only when GGML_MOE_STREAM_FUSED_UP_GATE=1, n_tokens==1, up/gate same type/shape, no bias/scale, and SILU.
source_notes.historical_profile: large 13056MiB batch cache improved up/gate cache hit rate to about 76%, but eval_tok_s stayed 0.8 and TTFT exceeded the accepted gate. Earlier profile split showed serial up+gate compute about 15.7 ms/call.
